title: The catering problem
narration: Axion Kitchen: quantum optimization for catering production. We completed the factory baselines in four and eight hours, both checked optimal. Our extension chooses shared batch yields, allocations, equipment, qualified workers and phase times. Cookers are machines, cleaning is setup, and departures are due dates. Freshness, calendars, outages and committed work constrain replanning. Complete meals come first, then waste, batches and changes.

title: Batch selection and scheduling constraints
narration: A bit selects a locally valid batch: its quantity, allocations, resources and times. Programs with the same anchor share demand, so a block chooses one program or idle. Cross-block penalties exclude clashes. In the code, product expands coverage products; coefficient span plus one sets the penalty. This cell uses thirty-two programs and three idle bits. Restricted portfolios can exclude better schedules.

title: Complete meals and food waste
narration: Main coverage times side coverage gives complete service; their sum minus twice the product counts unpaired food. Both coverages are linear in batch bits, so the objective stays quadratic. Each priority weight dominates all lower costs combined. For hard constraints, P equals the full objective coefficient span plus one. A violation therefore cannot beat any feasible schedule. This guarantees feasible ground states, not heuristic convergence.
live_action: Explain MS and waste first; after 60% the screen shows the range bound and penalty inequality. State the ground-state guarantee.
live_narration: Linear main and side coverage multiply into quadratic service and waste terms. Priority weights dominate lower costs. For hard constraints, the objective range is at most S. Set P to S plus one: every invalid state costs more than every feasible state. That proves the ground-state guarantee.
shot: Paired-coverage truth table, then the actual penalty-bound argument.
editor_cue: Switch to the proof at 53% in video (102.84 s), or 60% in live. Define S over the full bit domain, show P=S+1 and E(invalid)≥E(feasible)+1. A heuristic need not reach a ground state; R=B here.

title: QAOA results
narration: We selected the QAOA configuration on the cell and S0/S1. On held-out S2/S3, it finds the offered-pool optimum in all ten seeds at both budgets. Random-angle search also hits all ten on S2. At two hundred fifty-six evaluations, median optimum probability per shot is about eleven and twenty-two times random-angle search. Angles are optimized per instance. These restricted portfolios still exclude better full-grid schedules.

title: VQE comparison
narration: VQE uses Givens gates within blocks and controlled rotations between coupled blocks. With exact CVaR and adjoint gradients, median optimum probability is about twelve percent in both held-out cases. Budgets and shots differ from QAOA. The primary setup hits ten of ten and nine of ten seeds.
live_narration: VQE concentrates about twelve percent probability on the optimum in both cases. Its budgets and shot count differ from QAOA, so we show the methods separately.

title: VeloxQ inside the replanning loop
narration: VeloxQ now drives the replanning loop. Start with its own full plan, free two blocks, solve the conditional QUBO, and accept only a checked improvement. Across three widths, missed meal lots fall from nine to seven, eleven to six, and thirteen to seven. These runs used seventy-one submissions. Exact neighborhood controls match or improve final quality, and longer classical runs remain better. This demonstrates integration, not a speedup.
live_action: Follow the loop, then read the three starting and final missed-lot counts. Distinguish total adapter time from backend time; retain the exact-control and longer-CP comparison.

editor_cue: All block pairs are swept; each subproblem is capped at 40 variables. 71 submissions include five failures. Total adapter time is 565.4 s, backend time 126.784 s; these exclude the earlier cold-start generation. One seed per width. Exact controls match or improve final tuples; CP at 240 s / four workers has lower U at every width. Do not call this a matched-budget win.

title: What makes the choices difficult?
narration: The cell is deliberately small. Larger inputs generate eighteen thousand batch programs. Equipment, workers and paired demand couple their choices. We measure restriction loss and search quality separately.

title: Capacity: equipment or staff
kicker: THE SAME MODEL · A CAPACITY DECISION
narration: What should the kitchen buy? In the larger case, a third cooker leaves best-found service at ninety meals. A prep or packing helper raises it to one hundred ten: the existing worker handles both jobs. We changed one resource at a time, using equal classical budgets and two seeds. These are checked plans, not certified optima. Prices are still needed for an investment decision.
